title: bug: landLaneNode can time out or leave a dirty workspace while staffing the seeded policy step
description: Blocks task-6bafd3b9439640cba358dd6e79329c9d. On a fresh SHIPPED lane with {liveCredentials:"ABSENT", fakeGh:"SUCCESS"}, calling landLaneNode BEFORE creating the contract graph intermittently returns LANDING_BUDGET_SPENT with repeated policy.validate STAFFING_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED; another run continued into BASELINE_WORKSPACE_DIRTY. Repro: pnpm exec playwright test -c tests/e2e/control-room/playwright.config.ts contract-goal.spec.ts --grep "contract lane" (3.3m, 1 failed). Existing landingSeatDouble writes the same timestamped file for every staffed mission; landLaneNode uses maxAgents=2 and a continuous wrapper. Source/evidence and standalone reproduction will be attached in a comment.
definitionOfDone: A fresh seeded release-configured lane can call landLaneNode repeatedly and receives a real landing SHA with a clean workspace after teardown, with a committed regression that previously failed.
Policy/non-code staffing cannot rewrite a code node's submitted bytes or consume its landing signal; retain real wrapper/verifier/landing and no hand-seeded receipts.
Focused landing and dependent contract-goal browser arms pass under browser-e2e-gate; record executed spec count and exit status.

implementationPlan.description:
ESTABLISH THE RED. DoD 1 requires a regression that PREVIOUSLY FAILED, so the failing baseline is measured BEFORE any edit and quoted verbatim; without it the fix cannot be shown to fix anything.

The owner ruled the DoD-1 semantics (comment-c21629a4, governor-9af9af37, 2026-09-08T07:05Z): 'call landLaneNode repeatedly' means N INDEPENDENT FRESH SEEDED LANES, not repeat calls against one already-landed lane. No round-command replay and no completed-node lifecycle semantics are in scope. That is the only shape in which the reported intermittent can fail before the fix.

Write the reporter's minimal repro (task comment-6de16a94, quoted in the row description) as a THROWAWAY spec next to lane-landing.ts — `withDaemonBackedControlRoom({liveCredentials:'ABSENT', fakeGh:'SUCCESS'})`, `await landLaneNode(lane)`, assert `landed.ok` and an empty `git status --porcelain` in the lane workspace. Run it N times (N>=5) at the CURRENT tree under the browser-e2e-gate lease and record every outcome: how many returned LANDING_BUDGET_SPENT, how many BASELINE_WORKSPACE_DIRTY, how many passed, with the `[wrapper]`/`[lander]` transcript lines verbatim. An intermittent needs a denominator; 'it failed once' is not a baseline.

DELETE THE THROWAWAY before step 5 — step 5's `lane-landing.spec.ts` is the committed form. Record the exact command and the run tally in the step note; that tally is the 'previously failed' evidence DoD 1 asks for and QA will look for it.

If N runs all pass, DO NOT declare the bug absent and DO NOT proceed to a speculative fix: raise N, then say so in the note and on the row. The mechanism in step 3/4 is a real defect in this helper whether or not it reproduced today, but the DoD's 'previously failed' clause needs a measured red.

FIX THE SEAT DOUBLE (`landingSeatDouble`, lane-landing.ts:187). Two defects, both measured at HEAD 7fe37943.

1. IT IGNORES STDIN. The generated `.js` is `writeFileSync(<target>, 'landed at ' + new Date().toISOString())` and runs for EVERY staffed mission. `agent-spawner.ts:400` writes `request.mission` to stdin, so a `policy.validate` seat writes the code node's landing file — satisfying `landLaneNode`'s `existsSync` signal for a mission that never delivered the node. Make the child READ STDIN TO COMPLETION and write ONLY when the mission carries the target code-node clause from step 2. Anything else: write nothing, exit 0.

2. THE TIMESTAMP MAKES REPEAT WRITES UNSTABLE. The round's evidence package digests these bytes (`lane-review-round.ts` over `LANDED_PATH`); a restaff rewrites them with a new timestamp AFTER the digest was taken, so the node is refused and the item burns staffing attempts — the reported LANDING_BUDGET_SPENT with repeated STAFFING_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED. Make the content DETERMINISTIC and byte-stable across invocations. It must still DIFFER from the staffing baseline so the lander has something to commit; the file is absent at baseline, so a fixed body satisfies both.

The signature gains the target node ref. `landingSeatDouble` has exactly ONE caller (lane-landing.ts:216) — verified by `git grep -n landingSeatDouble` over the tree, whose only other hits are chat and task JSON — so no consumer is broken. But it IS exported: if you would change its exported shape in a way anything else could observe, stop and say so rather than widening the roster.

KEEP THE THREE-FILE BRIDGE EXACTLY AS DOCUMENTED: `.js` plus a `.cmd` for win32 and a `.sh` for posix, both delegating to the one `.js`, because `agent-spawn-invocation.ts` runs a win32 seat THROUGH cmd.exe as a command LINE. Do not collapse them; the module's own comment explains why, and `lane-multi-node-workspace.ts` (a peer row's file) copies the shape.

Stdin on the `.cmd` path is the risk this step must actually verify: prove the mission reaches the `.js` through cmd.exe on this host, rather than assuming the pipe survives. Step 2's arms go GREEN here. FENCED, per the owner ruling: no larger budgets, no hand-seeded receipts, no production authority edits.

FIX `landLaneNode` (lane-landing.ts:210). Three ordering defects, all measured, all in the same function.

1. THE TARGET IS RESOLVED AFTER THE SEAT WRITES. Today: spawn wrapper, wait for `existsSync(landedFile)`, THEN `laneCompiledNodeRef(scratch)`. So the file that releases the wait may have been written by any seat. RESOLVE THE COMPILED NODE REF BEFORE THE WRAPPER IS STARTED — it is available from `laneCompiledNodeRef(scratch)` the moment `retireSpecNode` has run, needs no wrapper, and step 3's seat double needs it to build the discriminator anyway. On null, refuse `NO_COMPILED_EXECUTION_NODE` with `laneCompiledNodeDiagnosis` exactly as now, before spawning anything.

2. IT ACCEPTS ANY COMMITTED NODE. `COMMITTED_LINE = /^\[lander\] (\S+): COMMITTED /mu` already CAPTURES the ref and the code discards it. Wait for a landing whose captured ref IS THE TARGET, and keep waiting otherwise — never credit another node's line, and never credit a `policy.validate` log line as a code landing. Keep the escaped `\]`: under the `u` flag a lone `]` is a SyntaxError thrown at IMPORT, which would take every spec importing this module down and make `test:e2e:browser` find no tests at all.

3. GIT HEAD IS READ WHILE THE WRAPPER IS STILL RUNNING. `laneWorkspaceIdentity(scratch.root)` sits inside the `try`; `killTree` is in the `finally`. A wrapper mid-baseline or mid-verify during that read is how a caller sees BASELINE_WORKSPACE_DIRTY. STOP THE TRACKED CHILDREN FIRST, then observe HEAD and cleanliness. The `finally` teardown STAYS — it must still fire on the refusing and throwing paths (epic rail 4) — so make the second teardown idempotent rather than moving it out.

A POLICY ITEM EXHAUSTING ITS ATTEMPTS IS EXPECTED, NOT THE FAILURE. With the seat double correctly ignoring non-target missions, `policy.validate` never moves and logs STAFFING_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED. That is why `LANDING_MAX_AGENTS = 2` exists — so it cannot starve the node that must land. The fix is that the code node lands ANYWAY; do not chase the policy log line, and do not raise a budget to silence it. A repair that makes the symptom vanish by widening a timeout is a rejectable defect, not a style note (owner ruling).

PRESERVE THE PUBLIC SHAPE. `LaneLanded`, `LaneLandingRefused`, `LANDING_BUDGET_MS`, `LANDED_PATH`, `laneCompiledNodeRef` and `laneCompiledNodeDiagnosis` have SIX consumers measured at HEAD: deploy-environment.spec.ts:55, deploy-fake-docker.spec.ts:33, deploy-migrations.spec.ts:69, lane-preview-arms.ts:29, lane-rollback-incident.ts:38, release-approval.spec.ts:19. None is in this row's roster, so none may need editing — if a change would force one, stop and report rather than taking a seventh path.

The file is 266 lines at HEAD, already past the 250 target. Keep it UNDER 400 and quote `wc -l`. Bringing it back under 250 would mean splitting a module six specs import and is NOT this row's job.

GATES (DoD 3), each standalone and foreground, each quoted with the count line that proves it EXECUTED. Exit 0 alone is not evidence: 'No test files found' and '0 passed' are also exit 0, so the discriminator is the printed `Test Files N passed` count — and for Playwright, the executed spec count and exit status, which DoD 3 names explicitly.

- `pnpm exec vitest run tests/e2e/control-room/lane-landing.test.ts` — the direct arms, seconds not minutes. This is the fast oracle for steps 2-4.
- `pnpm exec playwright test -c tests/e2e/control-room/playwright.config.ts lane-landing.spec.ts contract-goal.spec.ts` — the focused browser leg, under the browser-e2e-gate lease. `contract-goal.spec.ts` is the DEPENDENT arm DoD 3 requires and is the PEER'S UNTRACKED FILE: you RUN it as evidence, you do not own, edit or commit it. Name its owner and its untracked state in the record, and if it fails for a reason inside its own bytes rather than in the landing helper, attribute it there rather than absorbing it.
- `pnpm test` — the root lane, which DOES include `tests/**/*.test.ts` (vitest.config.ts include), so it covers this row's new direct arms. It covers NO apps/** file; say so.
- `pnpm typecheck` — and note that `tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json` exists and needs its own explicit typecheck if the root leg does not reach it. Verify which is true rather than assuming.
- `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`.
- `pnpm test:e2e:browser` — the full browser lane, for the six existing consumers of `landLaneNode` listed in step 4. This is the regression that matters most: the fix changes when the helper resolves its target and when it stops its children, and every one of those specs drives it.

PLAYWRIGHT INVERTS THE USUAL INSTINCT: a FAST pass is the green signature and a SLOW run is the red one waiting out a 30 s `toBeVisible`. Do not read a long run as thoroughness.

ATTRIBUTE FOREIGN RED, never hide it and never fabricate green. Path-attributed baseline: gate failures at the merge-base, gate failures at HEAD, subtract, intersect with this row's three owned paths; complete only when that intersection is EMPTY. Disclose foreign red verbatim with exact failing lines and paths. Acquire the shared gate lease rather than running a convoy beside other seats, and do not re-run a full suite repeatedly — it degrades every other seat's gate.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW AND THE MUTATION DRILL. Load `adversarial-self-review` and `regression-check`.

READ YOUR OWN DIFF AS THE BUG REPORTER:
- Does the seat double still write for a mission that merely MENTIONS the target ref somewhere in its instructions, rather than carrying the code-node claim clause? An over-broad match reintroduces the bug in a shape the arms do not cover.
- Does it write for the target on a SECOND staffing after the round's digest was taken — and are those bytes identical?
- Does `landLaneNode` still return the TARGET's sha if another node commits first, or does it now hang until the budget instead? Both are wrong in different ways; the arm must distinguish 'waited for the right one' from 'waited forever'.
- Is the `finally` teardown still reached on the refusing and throwing paths after the children were stopped early — and is the second kill idempotent rather than throwing on an already-dead child?
- Did the escaped `\]` in COMMITTED_LINE survive? An unescaped one is a SyntaxError at IMPORT that empties the whole browser lane.
- Did you raise ANY budget, seed ANY receipt, delete or reset ANY dirty bytes, or edit ANY production authority file? All four are owner-fenced rejections.
- Did any of the three owned paths touch the peer's untracked contract-goal files?

MUTATION DRILL, the arms' only real oracle. `git status --porcelain` the exact mutated paths FIRST. `lane-landing.test.ts` and `lane-landing.spec.ts` are NEW and UNTRACKED, so `git diff -- <path>` certifies NOTHING for them — empty before, during and after — and a silently unrestored mutation rides into the commit wearing a clean diff. Back each up OUT OF TREE under %TEMP% in a path carrying THIS TASK ID (a path keyed only on a worker id can hold a stale vintage whose SHA256 still matches after a restore that deleted the real work), hash the LIVE file at window-open, and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore. `git diff` is a valid restore proof for the TRACKED `lane-landing.ts` only. Do not drill on disk while holding a shared full-suite lease.

MUTATE THE PRODUCTION SURFACE AND CONFIRM RED, per the global rail: revert the stdin discriminator and confirm the policy arm goes red; restore the timestamp and confirm the byte-stability arm goes red; drop the target-ref match in COMMITTED_LINE and confirm the spec goes red. An arm that stays green under its own mutation is testing nothing.

Report every path you created or modified in `complete_step.modifiedFiles`.

🔒 OWNER RULING 07:07Z — **DoD 1 SEMANTICS ANSWERED: INDEPENDENT FRESH SEEDED LANES.** @architect-f362f7a6 asked this in the REPL and got no answer; I put it to the owner and they ruled. This comment is the authority. Recorded BEFORE the status change because BLOCKED→PLANNING nulls the block quartet; verbatim block record at the end.

**THE RULING.** "A fresh seeded release-configured lane can call `landLaneNode` repeatedly" means **each call gets its own fresh seeded lane** — N independent lanes, not N calls against one already-landed lane. You do NOT need to define round-command replay semantics or completed-node lifecycle for this row; both were the things that made the other reading expensive, and neither is now in scope.

**WHY THIS READING IS ALSO THE ONE THE BUG SUPPORTS**, so the DoD and the evidence agree rather than merely coexisting: the reported failure was "on a fresh SHIPPED `fakeGh=SUCCESS` lane **INTERMITTENTLY**" (task-6bafd3b9's blockedReason, evidence comment-6de16a94). An intermittent that appears across separate fresh runs is reproduced by repeating the fresh run, not by re-calling a lane that already succeeded. The regression this row owes is one that FAILS BEFORE THE FIX — DoD 1 says exactly that — and only the independent-lanes shape can fail that way.

**YOUR DIAGNOSIS IS ACCEPTED AS THE WORKING MECHANISM.** From your audit (comment-24801f4d) at HEAD aa438b78: `landLaneNode` resolves its target only AFTER any seat writes, accepts ANY `[lander] COMMITTED` node, and reads git HEAD before it kills the wrapper — while `agent-spawner.ts:400` writes `request.mission` to stdin and `agent-mission-text.ts:codeMission` opens with the exact code-node durable-claim header that `mission(policy.validate)` does not. That concretely permits a policy seat to consume the code node's landing signal, which is precisely the two symptoms reported (LANDING_BUDGET_SPENT with STAFFING_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED, and BASELINE_WORKSPACE_DIRTY). You said it needs red/green evidence rather than assertion — right, and DoD 1's "previously failed" regression is where you prove it.

**YOUR PROPOSED BOUNDED SCOPE IS APPROVED AS PROPOSED:** `tests/e2e/control-room/lane-landing.ts` plus NEW `lane-landing.test.ts` and `lane-landing.spec.ts` — three owned paths. Resolve the intended compiled node BEFORE spawn; target-match the actual mission header rather than an arbitrary substring in instructions; keep repeat writes byte-stable without truncation; ignore policy and other-node missions; wait for target-specific landing; stop tracked children before the final git clean and HEAD observation. Keep the native `.cmd`/`.sh` bridges.

⚠️ **AND THE FENCES YOU DREW YOURSELF, which I am reinforcing rather than relaxing:** no larger budgets, no hand-seeded receipts, no deletion or reset of dirty bytes, no production authority edits, and DoD 2 stands — policy/non-code staffing must not be able to rewrite a code node's submitted bytes or consume its landing signal, with the real wrapper, verifier and landing retained. A fix that makes the symptom disappear by widening a timeout would satisfy nobody and I would treat it as a rejectable defect, not a style note.

**STATUS: BLOCKED → PLANNING.** Both resume conditions in your block are now met — the semantics are ruled and the bounded repair is confirmed. Plan and submit. This is the root of a three-row chain (this row → task-6bafd3b9 → task-817d893f, the epic's browser release proof), so it is the highest-value row on the board right now; task-6bafd3b9 auto-unblocks the moment this reaches DONE.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
SCOPE WAS ALREADY SETTLED BY THE OWNER, AND I AM NOT REOPENING IT. governor-9af9af37's comment-c21629a4 (2026-09-08T07:05Z) records the owner's ruling on both open questions architect-f362f7a6 raised in comment-24801f4d: DoD 1's 'repeatedly' means N INDEPENDENT FRESH SEEDED LANES, and the bounded three-path scope (lane-landing.ts plus new lane-landing.test.ts and lane-landing.spec.ts) is approved as proposed. My job was to verify the diagnosis on disk and turn it into executable steps, not to re-litigate it. I verified every claim in that audit at HEAD 7fe37943 and all of them hold.

WHY THE DIRECT VITEST ARMS EXIST AT ALL, rather than proving everything through the browser lane. The reported repro is 3.3 minutes for one intermittent outcome, and step 1 needs N>=5 runs for a denominator. The seat double is a generated child process: spawning it and feeding it stdin is a seconds-long, fully deterministic test of the exact seam where the bug lives. tests/**/*.test.ts is already in the root vitest include and wrapper-lane.test.ts / daemon-children.test.ts are the precedent, so this costs no config change. The browser spec then proves the composed behaviour on real lanes; without the direct arms, every iteration of the fix costs minutes and the mutation drill becomes impractical.

REJECTED: raising LANDING_BUDGET_MS, SEAT_WRITE_BUDGET_MS or LANDING_STAFFING_ATTEMPTS. The owner fenced it explicitly and called a timeout-widening repair a rejectable defect. It is also wrong on the merits: the failure is a signal-attribution bug, and a bigger budget only lengthens the window in which the wrong seat can satisfy the wait.

REJECTED: making the policy item stop exhausting its attempts. With a correctly discriminating seat double, policy.validate never moves and logs STAFFING_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED; that is EXPECTED and is exactly why LANDING_MAX_AGENTS = 2 exists (the module's own comment at :~90 says so). The property to assert is that the code node lands anyway. Chasing the log line would mean either seeding policy work or shrinking the board, both fenced.

REJECTED: a fourth owned path to bring lane-landing.ts back under the 250-line target. It is 266 at HEAD, before this row touches it, and it is imported by six specs. Splitting it is a separate refactor with its own consumer census; this row keeps it under the 400 hard cap and says so.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD 7fe37943bf72b837205383ad0304e81a92ab66ea by architect-f6c5da87, 2026-09-08. Every claim in architect-f362f7a6's audit (comment-24801f4d, anchored at aa438b78) re-verified at this later HEAD and CONFIRMED.

THE THREE DEFECTS, WITH LINE ANCHORS IN tests/e2e/control-room/lane-landing.ts (266 lines).
(1) landingSeatDouble :187 generates `writeFileSync(<workspace>/landed-by-the-seat.txt, 'landed at ' + new Date().toISOString())` and reads NO stdin, so it runs identically for every staffed mission. Production agent-spawner.ts:400 does `child.stdin?.write(request.mission)` then `.end()`, so the mission IS available to discriminate on and is currently discarded. The timestamp also makes repeat writes byte-UNSTABLE, which matters because lane-review-round.ts digests exactly these bytes as SUBMITTED_BYTES — a restaff after the digest is taken invalidates the round.
(2) landLaneNode :210 waits on `existsSync(landedFile)` and only THEN calls `laneCompiledNodeRef(scratch)` — target resolved after any seat may have written. It then waits on `COMMITTED_LINE = /^\[lander\] (\S+): COMMITTED /mu`, which CAPTURES the ref and discards it, accepting any node's landing.
(3) `laneWorkspaceIdentity(scratch.root)` is called inside the `try`, while the wrapper is still alive; `killTree` runs only in the `finally`. A wrapper mid-baseline during that read is the reported BASELINE_WORKSPACE_DIRTY.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS EXACT AND MEASURED. apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts:110 — codeMission opens `You are a moe-next coding agent. You hold the durable claim on code node "${nodeRef}"`. Line 294 — mission() opens `You are a moe-next agent. You hold the durable claim on work item "${workItemId}" (command kind ${kind})`. Different sentence, different noun, and only the code form carries the node ref. Matching the code-node clause WITH the target ref is precise; matching a bare ref substring is not.

SINGLE CALLER. `git grep -n landingSeatDouble` over the tree returns lane-landing.ts:187 (definition) and :216 (the only call); every other hit is chat JSONL or task JSON. So the signature may take the target ref without breaking a consumer.

SIX CONSUMERS OF THE PUBLIC SHAPE, none in this row's roster and none expected to change: deploy-environment.spec.ts:55, deploy-fake-docker.spec.ts:33, deploy-migrations.spec.ts:69, lane-preview-arms.ts:29, lane-rollback-incident.ts:38, release-approval.spec.ts:19. That is why `pnpm test:e2e:browser` is a required regression leg rather than an optional one.

GATE TOPOLOGY. vitest.config.ts include is [adapters/**, packages/**, tests/**, tools/**] — tests/**/*.test.ts IS covered by root `pnpm test`, and apps/** is NOT covered by anything but the per-package legs. tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json exists and may need an explicit typecheck leg. Sibling direct-arm precedents in the same directory: wrapper-lane.test.ts (167), daemon-children.test.ts (144), harness.test.ts, journey-coverage.test.ts, daemon-lane-ledger.test.ts.

PEER DIRT, DO NOT TOUCH: contract-goal.spec.ts, lane-contract-goal.ts and lane-multi-node-workspace.ts are untracked in tests/e2e/control-room and belong to task-6bafd3b9 (worker-76f4ef35). DoD 3 requires RUNNING contract-goal.spec.ts as the dependent arm; it does not make those bytes this row's.

planningNotes.risks:
OVER-BROAD MISSION MATCHING reintroduces the bug in a shape the new arms would not catch: a mission that merely mentions the target ref (a diagnostic line, a hint payload) must NOT trigger the write. Match the code-node claim clause, not a bare ref substring.

STDIN THROUGH cmd.exe IS THE UNVERIFIED LINK. agent-spawn-invocation.ts runs a win32 seat through cmd.exe as a command LINE; the `.cmd` bridge must actually carry the piped mission to the `.js`. This is the one place the fix could work on posix and silently no-op on this Windows host — prove it rather than assume it, and note that a seat that reads nothing writes nothing, which turns into SEAT_NEVER_WROTE rather than a loud error.

WAITING FOREVER INSTEAD OF WAITING WRONG.
